title: Water activities at Pandan Reservoir suspended after crocodile sighting
Sustained Land plans 776-unit condo in Thomson Road enclave after 16-year launch drought
article:
It has been more than 16 years since a new private condominium was launched in the established residential enclave around Thomson Lane and Thomson Road in prime District 11. That drought is about to end.

A Sustained Land-led consortium, headed by property mogul Douglas Ong, has paid $578 million for a 203,073 sq ft site at 8 Thomson Lane, with plans for a 776-unit residential development rising more than 36 storeys and potentially above 40 storeys.

Given the site’s elevated position and largely low-rise surroundings, upper-floor units could have views towards MacRitchie Reservoir and the city skyline.

A property title search showed that SL Capital (9) Pte Ltd, an investment vehicle linked to Sustained Land, exercised the option to purchase the site for $578 million on Aug 11.

Including an estimated land betterment charge (LBC) of $436 million, based on rates effective from March 1, 2026, the effective land cost could exceed $1 billion. Based on a maximum potential gross floor area (GFA) of 781,830 sq ft, assuming the full 10% bonus GFA is secured, the land rate could work out to around $1,297 psf per plot ratio.

The consortium is acquiring a 105-year leasehold interest in the elevated site from seller Chequers Properties, which will continue to hold the underlying freehold title.

Last new launch was 368 Thomson in 2010

The last new private condo launched in this Thomson Road enclave was the 157-unit freehold 368 Thomson by City Developments Ltd (CDL) in July 2010.

At its initial launch, 80% of the first 120 units released were sold at an average price of $1,350 psf. The 36-storey development was completed in 2014.

Just six months earlier, CDL launched the 177-unit freehold Cube 8 at 376 Thomson Road in January 2010. The units were 85% sold on the first weekend at an average price of $1,250 psf. The 36-storey development was completed in 2013.

The latest resale at Cube 8 was for a 1,421 sq ft, three-bedroom unit on the 27th floor, which changed hands for $3.088 million ($2,173 psf), based on a caveat lodged in July 2026.

Before that, the 273-unit freehold Sky @ Eleven was launched in January 2007 at an average price of $975 psf. Its units were fully taken up within 30 hours. The development comprises four 42-storey blocks and was completed in 2010.

A little farther away, at Lorong 1 Toa Payoh in neighbouring District 12, the 777-unit The Orie provides a more recent new-launch benchmark. The project debuted in January 2025, when 86% of its units were snapped up on its launch weekend at an average price of $2,706 psf.

The 99-year leasehold condo is 95.5% sold to date at an average price of $2,701 psf, based on caveats lodged.

Sustained Land's largest project to date

Sustained Land will hold a 51% stake in the consortium purchasing the 8 Thomson Lane site, while Ong's wholly owned subsidiary and investment vehicle, SL Capital Ventures, will take a 27% stake. Construction and property development company Kay Lim Holdings will hold a 12% stake, while another joint-venture partner will take the remaining 10%.

The upcoming 776-unit project would be the largest residential development by unit count in which Sustained Land is the controlling shareholder.

Sustained Land was previously involved in the 731-unit The Poiz Residences , developed jointly with MCC Land and Greatview Development, although MCC Land led the joint venture.

Since its founding in 2006, Sustained Land and its wholly owned vehicles under SL Capital have developed about 20 residential projects, including 3 Cuscaden , Sky Everton and One Meyer .

Its latest launch was the 347-unit The Sen at Jalan Jurong Kechil. The 99-year leasehold condo is over 42% sold since its debut last November, with units fetching an average price of $2,349 psf, based on caveats lodged.

Invitation-only sale

An information memorandum obtained by EdgeProp Singapore showed that the 8 Thomson Lane site was offered for sale through a by-invitation-only private treaty exercise.

The site was marketed by joint agents Colliers and Cushman & Wakefield, with offers due by Oct 28, 2025. Negotiations took place thereafter.

ACRA documents show that the directors of Chequers Properties are also associated with entities linked to Lee Rubber Company, including Bukit Sembawang Estates, Kallang Development and Lee Pineapple Company. Lee Rubber Company was founded in 1931 by rubber magnate, industrialist and philanthropist Lee Kong Chian.

While the site is currently zoned "Hotel" with a gross plot ratio of 2.1, Chequers Properties has obtained in-principle URA approval for a change of use to "Residential" with a plot ratio of 3.5.

Before putting the site up for sale, Chequers Properties had applied to redevelop it for commercial use, with plans for a four-storey office podium and a 28-storey tower comprising offices and medical suites. URA issued a notice of refusal in August 2025.

From Chequers Hotel to EtonHouse

In September 2024, the seller obtained written permission to demolish a bungalow that had stood on the site since the early 1940s. It was said to be a grand mansion on the ridge overlooking Sungei Whampoa. Its address was formerly 418 Thomson Road before it was changed to 8 Thomson Lane.

From the 1950s until its closure in 1985, the property operated as Chequers Hotel for about three decades. By around 1994, the former hotel premises had become Europa Country Club Resort.

In 2014, EtonHouse International Education Group opened its campus at 8 Thomson Lane, where it remained until 2023.

Thomson Lane's next chapter

Several major infrastructure, housing and community projects are reshaping the surrounding neighbourhood. These include the North-South Corridor, targeted for completion in 2029, and the future Mount Pleasant MRT Station on the Thomson-East Coast Line, expected to open in tandem with surrounding residential developments.

The nearby Toa Payoh Integrated Development, a 12ha sports and community hub incorporating a stadium, indoor sports hall, aquatics centre, polyclinic and public library, is targeted for completion by 2030.

Under the 2025 Master Plan, the former Old Police Academy site at Mount Pleasant is also slated for redevelopment into a new residential precinct with about 6,000 public housing units. Together, these projects will transform the wider Thomson-Mount Pleasant-Toa Payoh area as Sustained Land prepares to redevelop 8 Thomson Lane for private housing.
